published.citation: Cáceres et al. 2011, dayside brightness temperature at 2.2 µm (NASA Exoplanet Archive emission table): 1995 +/- 40 K, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2011A&A...530A...5C/abstract

temperature.note: Its day side's brightness temperature is measured in secondary eclipse at 2.2 µm (European Southern Observatory (ESO) 8.2m Very Large Telescope (VLT) Melipal (UT3) at Paranal Observatory ISAAC) and nobody has imaged it, so the color is a Planck spectrum at its published temperature.
temperature.chosen: 3 measured of 4 rows; the smallest relative uncertainty, then the longest wavelength
temperature.facility: European Southern Observatory (ESO) 8.2m Very Large Telescope (VLT) Melipal (UT3) at Paranal Observatory ISAAC
